sanskrit: tato devarṣisahitaḥ saritaṃ gomatīm anu daśāśvamedhān ājahre jārūthyān sa nirargalān
english: Then, accompanied by divine sages along the river Gomatī, he performed ten unimpeded Aśvamedha sacrifices of the Jārūthya type.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca evam etan mahābāho rāmeṇāmitatejasā prāptaṃ vyasanam atyugraṃ vanavāsakṛtaṃ purā
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: O mighty-armed one, thus did Rāma of boundless splendor in former times endure that most severe affliction born of forest-exile.

sanskrit: mā śucaḥ puruṣavyāghra kṣatriyo 'si paraṃtapa bāhuvīryāśraye mārge vartase dīptanirṇaye
english: Do not grieve, O tiger among men; you are a warrior, O scorcher of foes. You travel a path supported by the strength of your arms, a path of blazing resolution.

sanskrit: na hi te vṛjinaṃ kiṃ cid dṛśyate param aṇv api asmin mārge viṣīdeyuḥ sendrā api surāsurāḥ
english: Not even the slightest fault is visible in you. Upon this path, even gods and demons together with Indra would despair.

sanskrit: saṃhatya nihato vṛtro marudbhir vajrapāṇinā namuciś caiva durdharṣo dīrghajihvā ca rākṣasī
english: Vṛtra was slain in battle by the Maruts and Indra the thunderbolt-wielder; so too was the invincible Namuci and the demoness Dīrghajihvā.

sanskrit: sahāyavati sarvārthāḥ saṃtiṣṭhantīha sarvaśaḥ kiṃ nu tasyājitaṃ saṃkhye bhrātā yasya dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: All purposes are fully achieved when one has allies. What indeed could be unconquered in battle for one whose brother is Dhanaṃjaya?

sanskrit: ayaṃ ca balināṃ śreṣṭho bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ yuvānau ca maheṣvāsau yamau mādravatīsutau ebhiḥ sahāyaiḥ kasmāt tvaṃ viṣīdasi paraṃtapa
english: And here is Bhīma, best among the mighty, of terrifying valor; and the two young great archers, the twins sons of Mādrī. With such allies, O scorcher of foes, why do you grieve?

sanskrit: ya ime vajriṇaḥ senāṃ jayeyuḥ samarudgaṇām tvam apy ebhir maheṣvāsaiḥ sahāyair devarūpibhiḥ vijeṣyasi raṇe sarvān amitrān bharatarṣabha
english: These men who could conquer even the army of Indra together with the Maruts — with these great bowmen as allies, gods in form, you too shall vanquish all your enemies in battle, O bull of the Bharata line.

sanskrit: itaś ca tvam imāṃ paśya saindhavena durātmanā balinā vīryamattena hṛtām ebhir mahātmabhiḥ
english: Furthermore, consider this: Draupadī was carried off by the wicked, powerful, and pride-maddened Jayadratha of Sindhu, yet these great-souled ones brought her back.

sanskrit: ānītāṃ draupadīṃ kṛṣṇāṃ kṛtvā karma suduṣkaram jayadrathaṃ ca rājānaṃ vijitaṃ vaśam āgatam
english: Kṛṣṇā Draupadī was recovered after that most difficult feat was accomplished, and King Jayadratha himself was conquered and brought under control.

sanskrit: asahāyena rāmeṇa vaidehī punar āhṛtā hatvā saṃkhye daśagrīvaṃ rākṣasaṃ bhīmavikramam
english: By Rāma, fighting virtually alone, Vaidehī was recovered after slaying in battle the ten-headed demon Rāvaṇa of terrifying valor.

sanskrit: yasya śākhāmṛgā mitrā ṛkṣāḥ kālamukhās tathā jātyantaragatā rājann etad buddhyānucintaya
english: His allies were monkeys, bears, and the Kālamukhas — beings of a different species entirely. Reflect on this with your mind, O king.

sanskrit: tasmāt tvaṃ kuruśārdūla mā śuco bharatarṣabha tvadvidhā hi mahātmāno na śocanti paraṃtapa
english: Therefore, O tiger among the Kurus, do not grieve, O bull of the Bharata line. Great-souled men like you do not grieve, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam āśvāsito rājā mārkaṇḍeyena dhīmatā tyaktvā duḥkham adīnātmā punar evedam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus consoled by the wise Mārkaṇḍeya, the king, casting off his sorrow, undepressed in spirit, spoke again as follows.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca nātmānam anuśocāmi nemān bhrātṝn mahāmune haraṇaṃ cāpi rājyasya yathemāṃ drupadātmajām
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I do not grieve for myself, O great sage, nor for these brothers, nor even for the loss of the kingdom, as much as I grieve for this daughter of Drupada.

sanskrit: dyūte durātmabhiḥ kliṣṭāḥ kṛṣṇayā tāritā vayam jayadrathena ca punar vanād apahṛtā balāt
english: Tormented by wicked men at the dice game, we were yet saved by Kṛṣṇā; and now she has again been forcibly carried off from the forest by Jayadratha.

sanskrit: asti sīmantinī kā cid dṛṣṭapūrvātha vā śrutā pativratā mahābhāgā yatheyaṃ drupadātmajā
english: Has any woman ever been seen or heard of — any woman with a parting, devoted to her husband, of great good fortune — who is the equal of this daughter of Drupada?

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca śṛṇu rājan kulastrīṇāṃ mahābhāgyaṃ yudhiṣṭhira sarvam etad yathā prāptaṃ sāvitryā rājakanyayā
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Hear, O king Yudhiṣṭhira, of the great good fortune of nobly born women — all of this as it was attained by Sāvitrī, the princess.

sanskrit: āsīn madreṣu dharmātmā rājā paramadhārmikaḥ brahmaṇyaś ca śaraṇyaś ca satyasaṃdho jitendriyaḥ
english: There was among the Madras a righteous king, supremely virtuous, devoted to Brahmins, a refuge for all, true to his word, and master of his senses.

sanskrit: yajvā dānapatir dakṣaḥ paurajānapadapriyaḥ pārthivo 'śvapatir nāma sarvabhūtahite rataḥ
english: A performer of sacrifices, a lord of charity, skillful, beloved of the townspeople and the countryside — that king was named Aśvapati, devoted to the welfare of all beings.

sanskrit: kṣamāvān anapatyaś ca satyavāg vijitendriyaḥ atikrāntena vayasā saṃtāpam upajagmivān
english: Endowed with forbearance, yet childless, truthful in speech, master of his senses — as his years advanced he was seized by sorrow.

sanskrit: apatyotpādanārthaṃ sa tīvraṃ niyamam āsthitaḥ kāle parimitāhāro brahmacārī jitendriyaḥ
english: For the purpose of begetting offspring he undertook a severe austerity: eating only a measured portion at the proper time, practicing celibacy, subduing his senses.

sanskrit: hutvā śatasahasraṃ sa sāvitryā rājasattama ṣaṣṭhe ṣaṣṭhe tadā kāle babhūva mitabhojanaḥ
english: Offering a hundred thousand oblations to Sāvitrī, O best of kings, he subsisted every sixth mealtime on scanty food.

sanskrit: etena niyamenāsīd varṣāṇy aṣṭādaśaiva tu pūrṇe tv aṣṭādaśe varṣe sāvitrī tuṣṭim abhyagāt svarūpiṇī tadā rājan darśayām āsa taṃ nṛpam
english: By this practice he continued for exactly eighteen years; when the eighteenth year was completed, Sāvitrī was pleased and, O king, appeared to that monarch in her own form.

sanskrit: agnihotrāt samutthāya harṣeṇa mahatānvitā uvāca cainaṃ varadā vacanaṃ pārthivaṃ tadā
english: Rising from the sacrificial fire, filled with great joy, the boon-giver spoke these words to that king.

sanskrit: brahmacaryeṇa śuddhena damena niyamena ca sarvātmanā ca madbhaktyā tuṣṭāsmi tava pārthiva
english: "By your pure celibacy, self-restraint, and discipline, and by your whole-hearted devotion to me, I am pleased with you, O king."

sanskrit: varaṃ vṛṇīṣvāśvapate madrarāja yathepsitam na pramādaś ca dharmeṣu kartavyas te kathaṃ cana
english: "Choose a boon, O Aśvapati, king of the Madras, whatever you desire. And you must never be negligent in matters of righteousness under any circumstances."

sanskrit: aśvapatir uvāca apatyārthaḥ samārambhaḥ kṛto dharmepsayā mayā putrā me bahavo devi bhaveyuḥ kulabhāvanāḥ
english: Aśvapati said: "This undertaking was begun by me out of desire for offspring, with longing for righteousness. May I have many sons, O goddess, who will uphold our lineage."

sanskrit: tuṣṭāsi yadi me devi kāmam etaṃ vṛṇomy aham saṃtānaṃ hi paro dharma ity āhur māṃ dvijātayaḥ
english: "If you are pleased with me, O goddess, this is the boon I choose. The twice-born tell me that progeny is the highest righteousness."

sanskrit: sāvitry uvāca pūrvam eva mayā rājann abhiprāyam imaṃ tava jñātvā putrārtham ukto vai tava hetoḥ pitāmahaḥ
english: Sāvitrī said: "O king, knowing already this intention of yours, the Grandfather was already addressed on your behalf beforehand, for the sake of sons."

sanskrit: prasādāc caiva tasmāt te svayaṃbhuvihitād bhuvi kanyā tejasvinī saumya kṣipram eva bhaviṣyati
english: "And by his grace, as ordained by the Self-Born, a radiant daughter will come to you on earth very soon, O gentle one."

sanskrit: uttaraṃ ca na te kiṃ cid vyāhartavyaṃ kathaṃ cana pitāmahanisargeṇa tuṣṭā hy etad bravīmi te
english: "You should say nothing further about this under any circumstance. I am pleased with the Grandfather's decree — this is what I tell you."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca sa tatheti pratijñāya sāvitryā vacanaṃ nṛpaḥ prasādayām āsa punaḥ kṣipram evaṃ bhaved iti
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Having agreed with "So be it" to Sāvitrī's words, the king beseeched her again: "May it be so quickly."

sanskrit: antarhitāyāṃ sāvitryāṃ jagāma svagṛhaṃ nṛpaḥ svarājye cāvasat prītaḥ prajā dharmeṇa pālayan
english: When Sāvitrī disappeared, the king returned to his own home; he dwelt in his own kingdom with joy, ruling his subjects by righteousness.

sanskrit: kasmiṃś cit tu gate kāle sa rājā niyatavrataḥ jyeṣṭhāyāṃ dharmacāriṇyāṃ mahiṣyāṃ garbham ādadhe
english: Then, as some time passed, that king, firm in his vows, begot a child upon his eldest queen, a righteous woman.

sanskrit: rājaputryāṃ tu garbhaḥ sa mālavyāṃ bharatarṣabha vyavardhata yathā śukle tārāpatir ivāmbare
english: That embryo in the Mālavī princess grew, O bull of the Bharata line, like the lord of stars in the bright fortnight of the sky.

sanskrit: prāpte kāle tu suṣuve kanyāṃ rājīvalocanām kriyāś ca tasyā muditaś cakre sa nṛpatis tadā
english: When the time came she gave birth to a lotus-eyed daughter; and the king joyfully performed the rites for her.

sanskrit: sāvitryā prītayā dattā sāvitryā hutayā hy api sāvitrīty eva nāmāsyāś cakrur viprās tathā pitā
english: She was given as a gift by a pleased Sāvitrī, born of oblations offered to Sāvitrī — so the Brahmins and her father gave her the name Sāvitrī.

sanskrit: sā vigrahavatīva śrīr vyavardhata nṛpātmajā kālena cāpi sā kanyā yauvanasthā babhūva ha
english: That princess grew like the goddess Śrī incarnate; and in time that maiden reached the bloom of youth.

sanskrit: tāṃ sumadhyāṃ pṛthuśroṇīṃ pratimāṃ kāñcanīm iva prāpteyaṃ devakanyeti dṛṣṭvā saṃmenire janāḥ
english: Seeing her with slender waist and broad hips, like a golden image, people thought: "Surely this must be a celestial maiden descended here."

sanskrit: tāṃ tu padmapalāśākṣīṃ jvalantīm iva tejasā na kaś cid varayām āsa tejasā prativāritaḥ
english: Yet no one sought her in marriage — she whose eyes were like lotus petals and who blazed with radiance — for they were repelled by her splendor.

sanskrit: athopoṣya śiraḥsnātā daivatāny abhigamya sā hutvāgniṃ vidhivad viprān vācayām āsa parvaṇi
english: Then, having fasted and bathed her head, having approached the divinities and offered into the fire according to rite, she had Brahmins recite on the holy day.

sanskrit: tataḥ sumanasaḥ śeṣāḥ pratigṛhya mahātmanaḥ pituḥ sakāśam agamad devī śrīr iva rūpiṇī
english: Then, taking the remaining flowers as blessed offerings from those great-souled ones, she went before her father like the goddess Śrī in human form.

sanskrit: sābhivādya pituḥ pādau śeṣāḥ pūrvaṃ nivedya ca kṛtāñjalir varārohā nṛpateḥ pārśvataḥ sthitā
english: She paid homage to her father's feet, first presented the remaining offerings, stood with joined palms, that noble-hipped woman, at the king's side.

sanskrit: yauvanasthāṃ tu tāṃ dṛṣṭvā svāṃ sutāṃ devarūpiṇīm ayācyamānāṃ ca varair nṛpatir duḥkhito 'bhavat
english: Seeing his own daughter, goddess-like in form, arrived at the bloom of youth yet unsought by suitors, the king was grieved.

sanskrit: rājovāca putri pradānakālas te na ca kaś cid vṛṇoti mām svayam anviccha bhartāraṃ guṇaiḥ sadṛśam ātmanaḥ
english: The king said: "Daughter, your time for being given in marriage has come, yet no one seeks me. Yourself seek out a husband equal to you in virtues."

sanskrit: prārthitaḥ puruṣo yaś ca sa nivedyas tvayā mama vimṛśyāhaṃ pradāsyāmi varaya tvaṃ yathepsitam
english: "Whatever man you desire, tell him to me; I shall reflect and bestow you. Choose as you wish."

sanskrit: śrutaṃ hi dharmaśāstre me paṭhyamānaṃ dvijātibhiḥ tathā tvam api kalyāṇi gadato me vacaḥ śṛṇu
english: "For I have heard this recited by twice-born men from the textbook of righteousness — and you too, O auspicious one, hear my words as I speak them."

sanskrit: apradātā pitā vācyo vācyaś cānupayan patiḥ mṛte bhartari putraś ca vācyo mātur arakṣitā
english: "A father who does not bestow her is blameworthy; a husband who does not love her is blameworthy; a son who does not protect his mother after the husband's death is blameworthy."

sanskrit: idaṃ me vacanaṃ śrutvā bhartur anveṣaṇe tvara devatānāṃ yathā vācyo na bhaveyaṃ tathā kuru
english: "Having heard these words of mine, hasten to seek a husband; act in such a way that the gods will not have cause to blame me."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca evam uktvā duhitaraṃ tathā vṛddhāṃś ca mantriṇaḥ vyādideśānuyātraṃ ca gamyatām ity acodayat
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Having thus spoken to his daughter, the king also instructed the elder counselors and urged the escort party: "Let them go."

sanskrit: sābhivādya pituḥ pādau vrīḍiteva manasvinī pitur vacanam ājñāya nirjagāmāvicāritam
english: She paid homage to her father's feet and, proud-spirited yet seemingly abashed, having received her father's command, departed without hesitation.

sanskrit: sā haimaṃ ratham āsthāya sthaviraiḥ sacivair vṛtā tapovanāni ramyāṇi rājarṣīṇāṃ jagām aha
english: She mounted a golden chariot and, surrounded by elder counselors, she visited the delightful forest-hermitages of the royal sages.

sanskrit: mānyānāṃ tatra vṛddhānāṃ kṛtvā pādābhivandanam vanāni kramaśas tāta sarvāṇy evābhyagacchata
english: Paying homage at the feet of the revered elders there, she visited all the forests in order, my son.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarveṣu tīrtheṣu dhanotsargaṃ nṛpātmajā kurvatī dvijamukhyānāṃ taṃ taṃ deśaṃ jagāma ha
english: Thus, distributing wealth at all the sacred fords, the princess went from place to place among the chief twice-born.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca atha madrādhipo rājā nāradena samāgataḥ upaviṣṭaḥ sabhāmadhye kathāyogena bhārata
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then the king, lord of the Madras, was met by Nārada and sat together with him in the midst of the assembly hall in conversation, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tato 'bhigamya tīrthāni sarvāṇy evāśramāṃs tathā ājagāma pitur veśma sāvitrī saha mantribhiḥ
english: Then, having visited all the sacred fords and the hermitages as well, Sāvitrī returned to her father's house together with the counselors.

sanskrit: nāradena sahāsīnaṃ dṛṣṭvā sā pitaraṃ śubhā ubhayor eva śirasā cakre pādābhivandanam
english: The auspicious one, seeing her father seated with Nārada, bowed her head and paid homage at the feet of both.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca kva gatābhūt suteyaṃ te kutaś caivāgatā nṛpa kimarthaṃ yuvatīṃ bhartre na caināṃ saṃprayacchasi
english: Nārada said: "Where had this daughter of yours gone, O king, and from where has she now returned? Why do you not bestow this young woman on a husband?"

sanskrit: aśvapatir uvāca kāryeṇa khalv anenaiva preṣitādyaiva cāgatā tad asyāḥ śṛṇu devarṣe bhartāraṃ yo 'nayā vṛtaḥ
english: Aśvapati said: "It is for this very purpose that she was sent out, and she has just now returned. Hear, O divine sage, about the husband she has chosen."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca sā brūhi vistareṇeti pitrā saṃcoditā śubhā daivatasyeva vacanaṃ pratigṛhyedam abravīt
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Urged by her father with "Speak fully about it," the auspicious Sāvitrī, receiving his word as if it were a divine command, spoke thus.

sanskrit: āsīc chālveṣu dharmātmā kṣatriyaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ dyumatsena iti khyātaḥ paścād andho babhūva ha
english: "There was among the Śālvas a righteous Kṣatriya, lord of the earth, known as Dyumatsena; he later became blind."

sanskrit: vinaṣṭacakṣuṣas tasya bālaputrasya dhīmataḥ sāmīpyena hṛtaṃ rājyaṃ chidre 'smin pūrvavairiṇā
english: "When he lost his sight, his kingdom was seized while his son was still young — a wise king — by a former enemy who exploited this vulnerability."

sanskrit: sa bālavatsayā sārdhaṃ bhāryayā prasthito vanam mahāraṇyagataś cāpi tapas tepe mahāvrataḥ
english: "He went to the forest together with his wife, who still cared for him like a child; entering the great forest, he practiced austerities of great vows."

sanskrit: tasya putraḥ pure jātaḥ saṃvṛddhaś ca tapovane satyavān anurūpo me bharteti manasā vṛtaḥ
english: "His son, born in the city but grown up in the hermitage, Satyavān — fitting to be my husband — I have chosen in my heart."

sanskrit: nārada uvāca aho bata mahat pāpaṃ sāvitryā nṛpate kṛtam ajānantyā yad anayā guṇavān satyavān vṛtaḥ
english: Nārada said: "Ah, what a great wrong has been done unknowingly by Sāvitrī, O king — that she has chosen this virtuous Satyavān!"

sanskrit: satyaṃ vadaty asya pitā satyaṃ mātā prabhāṣate tato 'sya brāhmaṇāś cakrur nāmaitat satyavān iti
english: "His father speaks truth, his mother speaks truth — therefore the Brahmins gave him this name: Satyavān, 'the truthful one.'"

sanskrit: bālasyāśvāḥ priyāś cāsya karoty aśvāṃś ca mṛnmayān citre 'pi ca likhaty aśvāṃś citrāśva iti cocyate
english: "As a child he loved horses; he used to make clay horses and drew horses in pictures — so he is also called Citrāśva, 'the one of painted horses.'"

sanskrit: rājovāca apīdānīṃ sa tejasvī buddhimān vā nṛpātmajaḥ kṣamāvān api vā śūraḥ satyavān pitṛnandanaḥ
english: The king said: "Is he then radiant, wise, that son of a king? Is Satyavān, who delights his father, also patient and valiant?"

sanskrit: nārada uvāca vivasvān iva tejasvī bṛhaspatisamo matau mahendra iva śūraś ca vasudheva kṣamānvitaḥ
english: Nārada said: "He is radiant as Vivasvān, equal to Bṛhaspati in intellect, valiant as great Indra, and endowed with patience like the earth."

sanskrit: aśvapatir uvāca api rājātmajo dātā brahmaṇyo vāpi satyavān rūpavān apy udāro vāpy atha vā priyadarśanaḥ
english: Aśvapati said: "Is Satyavān, the prince, also a giver, devoted to Brahmins, handsome, noble-spirited, or of pleasant appearance?"

sanskrit: nārada uvāca sāṅkṛte rantidevasya sa śaktyā dānataḥ samaḥ brahmaṇyaḥ satyavādī ca śibir auśīnaro yathā
english: Nārada said: "In giving, according to his ability, he equals Rantideva of Saṅkṛti's line; devoted to Brahmins and truthful in speech like Śibi of Uśīnara's line."

sanskrit: yayātir iva codāraḥ somavat priyadarśanaḥ rūpeṇānyatamo 'śvibhyāṃ dyumatsenasuto balī
english: "Noble as Yayāti, of pleasant appearance like the Moon — in beauty, Dyumatsena's powerful son is unsurpassed, a match for the Aśvins."

sanskrit: sa dāntaḥ sa mṛduḥ śūraḥ sa satyaḥ sa jitendriyaḥ sa maitraḥ so 'nasūyaś ca sa hrīmān dhṛtimāṃś ca saḥ
english: "He is self-restrained, gentle, and brave; truthful and master of his senses; friendly and free from envy; modest and steadfast."

sanskrit: nityaśaś cārjavaṃ tasmin sthitis tasyaiva ca dhruvā saṃkṣepatas tapovṛddhaiḥ śīlavṛddhaiś ca kathyate
english: "In him there is ever directness, and his steadfastness is unwavering. In brief, this is what is said of him by those venerable in austerity and those venerable in character."

sanskrit: aśvapatir uvāca guṇair upetaṃ sarvais taṃ bhagavan prabravīṣi me doṣān apy asya me brūhi yadi santīha ke cana
english: Aśvapati said: "You describe him to me as endowed with all virtues, O blessed one. Tell me also of his faults, if there are any here."

sanskrit: nārada uvāca eko doṣo 'sya nānyo 'sti so 'dya prabhṛti satyavān saṃvatsareṇa kṣīṇāyur dehanyāsaṃ kariṣyati
english: Nārada said: "He has one flaw and no other: Satyavān, from this very day, will exhaust his lifespan and lay down his body within a year."

sanskrit: rājovāca ehi sāvitri gaccha tvam anyaṃ varaya śobhane tasya doṣo mahān eko guṇān ākramya tiṣṭhati
english: The king said: "Come, Sāvitrī, go and choose another, O lovely one. His one great flaw overshadows and overcomes all his virtues."

sanskrit: yathā me bhagavān āha nārado devasatkṛtaḥ saṃvatsareṇa so 'lpāyur dehanyāsaṃ kariṣyati
english: "As the blessed Nārada, honored by the gods, has told me: within a year that short-lived one will lay down his body."

sanskrit: sāvitry uvāca sakṛd aṃśo nipatati sakṛt kanyā pradīyate sakṛd āha dadānīti trīṇy etāni sakṛt sakṛt
english: Sāvitrī said: "A lot falls but once; a daughter is given but once; and one says 'I give' but once — these three things happen only once, each only once."
